To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Linked REST APIs can be used to build RESTful services that are semantically integrated, and the middleware we propose is capable of automatically composing REST API calls to answer queries expressed in SPARQL.

we have developed an approach for REST service integration based on Linked data models and that we have demonstrated the usefulness of our approach with an application that integrates REST services to support research-data management.

we have proposed an architecture for REST service integration based on Linked data models, developed an RDF model for characterising the access control protocols of REST APIs and the quality and provenance of the data they provide, and built a prototype that implements the framework and shows its usefulness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework for the integration of REST services based on Linked Data principles.
the following questions: (1) Can we automatically integrate REST services based on Linked Data?
the development of middleware that can support the integration and composition of REST APIs based on their Linked Data descriptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the framework we propose is an important contribution towards a semantic REST API integration middleware that can automatically generate compositions of REST APIs, based on the data models and access protocols of the underlying APIs.
the Linked REST API integration middleware is a useful framework that allows the integration of REST services in the Linked Data context.

we have developed a conceptual framework for integrating REST APIs based on Linked Data, and have demonstrated the usefulness of this approach in the context of an application for research-data management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed middleware can be seen as a semantic layer on top of existing REST APIs, and can help developers to build applications that are more flexible and reusable.
we have developed a framework for REST service integration based on Linked-Data models, and a middleware that can use the models to automatically compose API calls in response to data queries.
our framework provides a solution to the problem of REST API integration by enabling the use of Linked Data formalisms to characterize the data and access protocols of the services.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, with the right tools and a bit of effort, it is possible to integrate a wide range of data resources, even those with different data models, into an interoperable, queryable, and reusable Linked Data service, with a minimum of effort.
the Linked Data model can be used to integrate and compose data exposed via REST services in a principled and reusable manner.

Linked Data models can be used to integrate REST APIs, and that the use of such models can be supported with a middleware that is capable of automatically composing API calls and enforcing access control.
